## Findings
- claim-1: The lower-adjoined family generates \(J_v\), and the 2024 theorem proves its minimality over \(\mathbb Z\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235]
- claim-2: The claimed no-syzygy theorem is deduced from Theorem 4.4; it is the essential input used to upgrade minimal generation to integral independence. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 790-831]
- claim-3: Assuming that no-syzygy theorem, the lower-adjoined residues are an integral homogeneous basis of \(J_v/A_+J_v\): a homogeneous kernel relation is exactly a prohibited syzygy; hence no torsion remains. The grading is Schur degree (ordinary cohomological degrees are twice these).
- claim-4: The first missing certificate is the large-\(N\) descent in Theorem 4.4: one needs \[ P\bigl(\operatorname{Lin}_{\widehat\varphi}(\tau)\bigr)\in \operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{\operatorname{Lin}_{\varphi}(\nu): \nu\in\operatorname{Dec}_{\varphi}\text{ wide}\} \] for every wide \(\tau\in\operatorname{Dec}_{\widehat\varphi}\), where \(P\) kills the enlarged variables. This is not supplied.
- claim-5: Lemma 4.3 verifies only \(P(\operatorname{Lin}_{\widehat\varphi}(\widehat\nu)) =\operatorname{Lin}_{\varphi}(\nu)\) for originally indexed \(\nu\); it does not control the additional wide enlarged equations. Therefore inconsistency of the enlarged system does not, by itself, imply inconsistency of the original subsystem. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 777-818]
- claim-6: Conditional on the lower integral-basis result, conjugation is otherwise sound: \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) sends \(I_{r,q}\) to \(I_{q,r}\), preserves Schur degree and \(A_+\), and sends the interval above \(i^j\) to that above \(j^i\). The parameter translation \[ v^\vee=v_{q,\ q+j-i,\ q-i+1,\ n},\qquad (i^\vee,j^\vee,a^\vee,b^\vee)=(j,i,a,b) \] satisfies the bigrassmannian inequalities.
- claim-7: Under that conditional quotient isomorphism, conjugating \((j^i,\rho)\), \(\rho\subseteq b^a\), gives \[ (j^i,\rho)'=(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{\,j-b}), \] exactly the right-adjoined family. Its generation follows from graded Nakayama since \(A_+\) is nilpotent in \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\).
## Strategy
The requested target is established.

The first defective dependency is the large-\(N\) step at [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 803-818]: inconsistency does not generally survive specialization. Repair it as follows. Let \(q=n-r\), \(C=(q-i)^j\), and let \(P\) retain only \(A_{\lambda,\theta}\) with \(\lambda\subseteq b^a,\theta\subseteq C\). For an enlarged wide row \(\tau\), write \(\tau_B=B\subseteq b^a\) and \(\tau_R=R\ne\varnothing\), with \(|B|+|R|=N\).

If \(R\subseteq C\), the partition
\[
\nu=(i+R_1,\ldots,i+R_j,B_1,\ldots,B_a)
\]
is an original wide decomposable partition and \(\tau=\widehat\nu\); hence Lemma 4.3 gives
\[
P(\operatorname{Lin}_{\widehat\varphi}(\tau))
=\operatorname{Lin}_{\varphi}(\nu).
\]
If \(R\nsubseteq C\), every retained wide-row coefficient contains
\[
c_{\lambda,\mu}^{B}c_{\mu,R}^{\theta},\qquad \theta\subseteq C.
\]
Since \(c_{\mu,R}^{\theta}\ne0\) requires \(R\subseteq\theta\), all such coefficients vanish, so \(P(\operatorname{Lin}_{\widehat\varphi}(\tau))=0\). Enlarged tall rows are exactly embedded original tall rows. Thus a solution of the original system, extended by zero on discarded variables, would solve the enlarged system, contradicting its small-\(N\) inconsistency.

Consequently the no-syzygy input applies integrally. Generation gives a surjection from the free group on the lower-adjoined family to \(J_v/A_+J_v\); a homogeneous kernel element is a prohibited syzygy. Hence the lower family is an integral homogeneous basis, so no torsion occurs.

Partition conjugation is an integral Schur-basis permutation
\[
\Lambda/I_{r,q}\cong\Lambda/I_{q,r},
\quad \bar s_\lambda\mapsto\bar s_{\lambda'},
\]
preserving Schur weight and \(A_+\). It sends \(i^j\) to \(j^i\), and
\[
v^\vee=v_{q,q+j-i,q-i+1,n},
\qquad(i^\vee,j^\vee,a^\vee,b^\vee)=(j,i,a,b),
\]
satisfies the bigrassmannian inequalities. Conjugating the lower basis gives exactly
\[
(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{\,j-b}),
\]
the right-adjoined family. Nilpotence of \(A_+\) in the finite Grassmannian quotient gives its generation; its quotient basis proves irredundancy.

## Gaps
No unresolved gap remains for the requested three conclusions after the displayed large-\(N\) repair. The source’s minimality theorem alone would not imply torsion-freeness; the integral conclusion uses the repaired no-syzygy argument.

Schur weight is the grading used above; ordinary cohomological degree is twice this weight.
